summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. Both IFilterManagerService and AvaloniaFilterManagerService are clean, minimal, and correctly follow the AvaloniaConnectionEditorService pattern. Fix-Forward applied: explicit event handler unsubscription via try/finally to prevent the closed dialog Window from being held in memory via the caller-owned ViewModel's event after ShowAsync returns.

comments.note: AvaloniaFilterManagerService.ShowAsync: replaced anonymous lambda with a named EventHandler (closeHandler) and wrapped ShowDialog in try/finally to unsubscribe it afterward. The ViewModel is passed in from the caller and may outlive the dialog — without unsubscription, the closed Window stays in memory as long as the ViewModel lives via the captured closure. The reference pattern (AvaloniaConnectionEditorService) creates the VM locally so it goes out of scope naturally; this fix closes the equivalent gap for the externally-supplied VM case.

IFilterManagerService.cs is well-structured. The interface correctly returns Task (not Task<T>) since filters produce no typed result, and the pre-initialized ViewModel parameter pattern is appropriate given the complex initialization state the filter manager requires.

The CancellationToken parameter is accepted but not forwarded to ShowDialog — this is consistent with AvaloniaConnectionEditorService and intentional; Avalonia's ShowDialog does not support cancellation tokens directly.
